newsitem.title: USA: Wis. committee adds $215 mln settlement to budget.
newsitem.headline: Wis. committee adds $215 mln settlement to budget.

text.p: Wisconsin's proposed fiscal 1998 budget advanced by the Joint Finance Committee includes $215 million to settle lengthy litigation over the state's retirement systems, a legislative fiscal analyst said Monday.

Inclusion of funding for the proposed settlement now under discussion would eliminate the need to issue operating notes later in the year to cover that expense, said Tony Mason, an analyst with the Wisconsin Legislative Fiscal Bureau.
Wisconsin is scheduled to sell $300 million of operating notes competitively on June 25 to cover short-term funding needs during fiscal 1998, which begins on July 1.

A preliminary official statement for that sale noted that the proposed settlement had not been included in Gov. Tommy Thompson's executive budget recommendations and a state review of cash-flow needs might lead to issuance of additional operating notes in that event.

Wisconsin Supreme Court justices in January upheld lower court rulings that a state transfer of $230 million as a special performance dividend for older pensioners in 1987 violated the state constitution and remanded the matter for further proceedings before a Dane County Circuit Court judge.
Attorneys defending the state in the litigation and those representing state engineers and executives challenging the transfer have not reached a final resolution of the dispute, Mason said.
The attorneys were in a hearing before Dane County Judge Angela Bartell on Monday involving the matter, a clerk for the judge said.
